draft.method: per face on the B-rep: a plane's angle to the pull exactly, a cylinder's or cone's whose axis runs along the pull exactly (zero, the half-angle), any other face the least over points sampled on it and along its edges; faces at or above wall_limit_deg are not walls. feature: turn for a face the parting line crosses that only turns through the pull (a round, a sphere: under 0.25 of its area has less than 0.5 deg), which is no wall along it; half_depth_mm: how deep the face runs in one mold half (either side of the parting plane) with its least draft; width_mm: its greatest extent square to the pull; broad: a wall of the part's shell, at least 10 nominal walls wide

undercuts.method: points sampled on every face, each shot along the way its face opens with exact rays (a zero-draft point both ways); a blocked point is trapped, but one standing in a crevice (another face within three ray offsets straight out of it); trapped faces that touch are one group, split where its trapped points lie apart: each piece a feature, released by rays along slides (its own faces' directions and eight round the parting plane; angled only where no plain ones free it), a lifter's short move, or a collapsible core's; one nothing releases that rests on few points is read again on denser ones; each part is tested against itself

thickness.method: rolling ball: at each point sampled on the faces, the diameter of the largest ball touching the surface there that stays inside the part, never more than the exact ray straight through; a face's thickness_mm is the area median of its points, min_mm the 10th percentile, max_mm the most; the nominal wall is the area median over the part, leaving out the points held by a face round a convex edge (they read low); feature: a rib's or a boss's face (their rules judge them, the wall's range does not), else wall; broad_wall_mm: the face's own wall (the area median of its own balls, no neighbour's and no refined point) where it bounds a broad wall -- it and the face across (across) each at least 10 of that wall wide (width_mm: its second extent, or four times its area over its outline if less) -- which is what the floor of walls too thin to fill judges

transitions.method: each step read on its stepped side: two parallel faces facing the same way whose walls differ by a quarter of the nominal or more and by about their offset (one face behind both), joined by a chain of faces (a pad's side, a chamfer, a fillet); transition_ratio is the chain's run across (square to the faces) over the change in wall, so a vertical step reads 0 and a chamfer its run over its rise; the item names the chain's first face, min_mm and max_mm the two walls, at_xyz a point on each seam. A free-form face, which no such faces bound, is read by the rolling ball: the steepest change between two of its points within four sample spacings whose walls differ by half the nominal (basis: ball)

projection.method: the part triangulated on its B-rep and projected on the parting plane; the area is the cells of a raster 2000 across the part whose centres a triangle covers, good to area_error_mm2 (half the outline's cells)

parting.method: the outline's silhouette: edges where a face opening along the pull meets one opening against it, zero-draft walls and curved faces turning through the pull, those within three raster cells of the projected outline; one flat plane takes them when every edge and turn is level (to tolerance_mm) at one height that every wall spans

envelope.method: spans of the part's projection on the parting plane (along its axes), its depth along the pull, and the farther of its depths above and below the parting plane

pull_check.method: the measured pull's own figures against the part's own directions (those most of its surface is square to or turns about, and its principal axes), each read only as far as it can still do better (measured: draft, then trapped, released, full): fewer features nothing releases, then less trapped area, fewer actions, less wall without draft, a flat parting

clamp.factor_source: Moldminds, Clamp force calculator (material tonnage factors) (https://moldminds.com/clamp-force-calculator/)
clamp.method: projected area (in2) x tonnage factor (tons/in2) x cavities x (1 + safety); the area is the part's alone (runners and sprues add to it), the factor a molder's table, not a resin supplier's cavity pressure: an estimate for choosing a press, not a mold design

rules.title: cad general rules
rules.note: general practice from published design guides, no shop's limits: draft (0.5 deg on vertical faces, 2 deg recommended), a wall table per resin, corner, transition, undercut, snap-fit and root guidance, rib and boss proportions -- recommendations, warnings. The errors are floors, what a general molder sends back: a feature nothing releases; and cad's own, each rule's note says so -- a broad shell wall with under 0.01 deg of draft for each millimetre it runs past 10 in one mold half (0.25 deg at most), a broad wall under 0.5 of the resin's recommended minimum, a projected area no press built clamps (over 10000 US tons at 1 ton/in2). Not judged: a living hinge, a thread, the gate and the ejection; the extra draft a textured or a tall wall takes (Hubs: 1 deg more per 25 mm over 50 mm; 1-2 deg more for texture), a shut-off's draft (Protolabs: 3 deg at least). A press's and a mold's own limits are compared with the measurements
